conclusion: The prior fix round's four attempts, plus this round's attempt 5, all reproduced an identical near-zero-CPU hang on QuantConnect.Common despite testing MSBuild node count, build-server persistence, TMPDIR isolation, analyzer cost, and terminal-logger/stdin handling. Precisely measuring attempt 5's cgroup/proc CPU accounting (rather than judging by inspection) still showed the same ~5.6s-total-CPU-over-230s+-wall-time signature, ruling out --disable-build-servers as the fix. DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=2 -- constraining the .NET runtime's own GC-heap and thread-pool sizing, independent of any MSBuild flag -- resolved it on both an isolated single-project probe (attempt 6) and the full solution (attempt 7).

diagnostic_evidence.referenced_package_dlls_valid: Spot-checked cloneextensions/fasterflect/sharpziplib/mathnet.numerics/mcmaster.extensions.commandlineutils DLLs referenced by Common's compile response file: all valid PE32 .NET assemblies, plausible sizes, not truncated/corrupt.

diagnostic_evidence.cpu: cgroup cpu.max ~2200000/100000 (about 22 cores, unthrottled) in every attempt; cpu.stat nr_throttled stayed 0. Attempt 5 precisely measured usage_usec=5,671,892 over 230+s wall time (~2.5% duty cycle); attempts 6/7 sustained 60-210% CPU continuously once the fix was applied.
diagnostic_evidence.disk: No process observed in D (uninterruptible disk sleep) state during any attempt.
diagnostic_evidence.thread_state_signature: Every hung attempt (1, 2, 3, 5) showed the same pattern when inspected: dozens of threads in S (sleeping) on futex_do_wait and exactly one in R (running) with near-zero cumulative CPU; attempt 5 confirmed this precisely via /proc/[pid]/task/*/status (54 threads, 53 S, 1 R) and /proc/[pid]/wchan=futex_do_wait on the top-level dotnet/MSBuild/csc processes.
diagnostic_evidence.host_contention_at_fix_time: At the time of attempts 5-7, `ps --sort=-pcpu` showed a concurrent, unrelated lane's vllm process using ~98% of one core plus several `bash -c while :; do :; done` busy-loops at ~16% each (load average ~10.7 of 24 cores) -- this host is shared across concurrent W1 lanes; DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=2 is a robust mitigation for that shared-host condition, not merely a one-off.
diagnostic_evidence.consistent_reproduction_point: Every hung attempt (including this round's attempt 5) reached the identical point: Logging/Configuration/Compression always complete in seconds; the hang begins immediately after QuantConnect.Common's CoreCompile writes its MSBuild cache files and starts csc.

root_cause: Not MSBuild node count, build-server/VBCSCompiler persistence, TMPDIR/analyzer/terminal-logger/stdin handling, memory, disk, or a hard deadlock. The .NET runtime (dotnet/MSBuild/csc, all managed processes) defaults its GC heap count and thread-pool sizing to the visible processor count (24 on this host); under concurrent load from other lanes sharing the same 24 cores, the resulting large number of futex-synchronized worker/GC threads apparently could not get scheduled fairly enough to make forward progress on this WSL2 host, producing a near-zero-CPU stall that looks identical to a deadlock (S-state threads, one R thread, no OOM/throttle/D-state) but resolves once DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT caps the runtime's own thread/heap fan-out to a small number.
limitations: Root-cause diagnosis rests on a single successful reproduction path (DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=2 on both an isolated single-project probe and the full solution) plus five independently reproduced hangs without it; a controlled sweep (e.g. DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=1,2,4,8 with and without host contention) was not run, so the exact contention threshold is not established -- only that 2 works and unset does not, on this shared host, at this observed load.

The existing tools/lean-985ef30 and tools/lean-985ef30-remediation roots were not rebuilt or compared against for this diagnosis; the 7730-warning match against resolution.md's recorded count is a strong but indirect cross-check, not a rebuild of those roots.

This is a local integration build on one pinned commit plus the recorded remediation patch, not a general fix for QuantConnect/Lean's upstream build, and not evidence that every WSL2/many-core host exhibits this stall.
